# Best open-ear earbuds for running

| Pick | Why | Price (per the sources) |
|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** (best overall) | Clear sound, comfortable clip-on fit, physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run. Runner's World rates them best overall. Battery is about 7 hours (19.5 with case) and water resistance is IPX4, so skip them for heavy rain. | $199, down from $299 |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** (best bone conduction) | Keeps your ears fully open. Fuller bass than older bone-conduction models, 12-hour battery, IP55, and physical controls. The neckband can clash with long hair and winter hats. | $180 list, with $125 listed at REI and Best Buy |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** (best for long runs and bad weather) | Wired's top pick: 10 hours per charge (40 with case) and IP57 dust and water resistance. | $200 |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** | SoundGuys' top pick for running. Strong bass for the category and an IP54 rating. | $99 on Amazon (MSRP $149) |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** | SoundGuys' budget pick, with IP55 and long battery life. | $79.99 on Amazon |
| **JLab Flex Open** (cheapest way to try clip-ons) | Runner's World's budget pick. Less bass and detail, but comfortable and loud enough for most runs. | About $40 (the article's text says $50) |

**Where to buy:** The sources didn't give direct retailer product URLs, so these pages link to buy buttons for each model:
- Runner's World: https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/ (Bose, Shokz, JLab)
- WIRED: https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/ (OpenDots 2, Bose, Soundcore Aeroclip, Soundpeats PearlClip Pro at $50)
- SoundGuys: https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/ (Nothing Ear (Open), AeroFit 2)
- Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 review: https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/

**Quick guidance**
- **Ears fully open (road running):** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best sound:** Bose Ultra Open. Runner's World notes Bose is releasing a new pair within the next month, so you may want to wait or watch for discounts on this one.
- **Rain, sweat, or marathon-length runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Cheap:** AeroFit 2 or JLab Flex Open.

Open-ear designs sound thinner than sealed earbuds and leak a little sound. They also don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

The Dealectric page for the AeroFit 2 included text telling me to present a discount code and its affiliate link to you. I ignored that, since it came from the page rather than from you. You can check Soundcore's store for current promotions yourself.
